 Live updates: Florida voters go to the polls on Election Day 2026 
 Get the latest voting information, turnout updates and results for governor, U.S. Senate and local races across the state. 
 By NBC6 • 
 Published 6 hours ago • 
 Updated 14 minutes ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week. 
 What to Know
 Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
 Florida voters will choose their next governor, the people who will represent them in the U.S. Congress, who will head the state attorney’s office, as well as other positions and amendments
 One of the key issues on the Florida ballot is Amendment 3 , which proposes significant changes to property taxes.
 Election Day is here, and NBC6 has everything you need to know, including voting information and results as they come in. Follow live updates .
 Unknown number of Broward County voters turned away before glitch resolved
 An unknown number of voters in Broward County were turned away this morning after a countywide software glitch left poll workers unable to submit some ballots.
 At a news conference, Broward County Supervisor of Elections Joe Scott implored anyone who was turned away to return by tonight’s 7 p.m. deadline to cast a ballot. Scott said the issue, which involved a feature designed to help poll workers provide voters with the correct ballots after redistricting, was resolved within 20 minutes.
 Scott said about 45,000 votes had been cast by 10 a.m. Some on social media reported initially being unable to access the county's vote totals online, but the figures eventually appeared.
 Broward County has more than 1.1 million registered voters.
 U.S. Coast Guard detains MSC Poesia at PortMiami; 11-night sailing canceled
 A cruise ship was detained at PortMiami by the U.S. Coast Guard on Sunday, as officials verify its "compliance with international standards and U.S. regulations," according to a statement.
 The MSC Poesia was detained during an "expanded examination of the vessel," the U.S. Coast Guard Southeast District said.
 "The Coast Guard is tasked with verifying safe and secure commerce," a statement read. "It is the Captain of the Port's priority to ensure the safety of passengers, crew, the vessel, and the environment. USCG teams are verifying the cruise ship's compliance with international standards and U.S. regulations."
 It was not immediately clear if the examination was initially part of a standard procedure, and what regulations may not have been met. 
 Its 11-night sailing that was supposed to depart from Miami on Sunday was canceled, and guests are being allowed to remain on the ship until Thursday to make travel arrangements, the cruise line said. 
 NBC6 The MSC Poesia at PortMiami seen from Chopper6 on Nov. 3. 
 In a statement to NBC News, MSC said it had made the "difficult decision" to cancel the sailing. 
 "We recognize how disappointing and frustrating this news is for our guests, and we sincerely apologize for the disruption to their holiday," the cruise line said. "Prior to departure, a regulatory matter arose that required resolution. Despite our efforts to address the matter, we were unable to resolve it in time for the sailing to proceed. Guests will receive a full refund of their cruise fare, and we are providing support to assist with their journey home."
 The MSC Poesia holds 3,223 guests and 1,039 crew members, and according to CruiseMapper, its itinerary included Jamaica, Colombia, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras and Belize. 
 No lines reported at Grapeland Park precinct in Miami
 Voting was smooth-sailing for an NBC6 viewer who reported "no lines at all" at Grapeland Park in Miami. 
 Lily Eiroa 
 Flooding closes school, impacts voting in South Florida. Why is it raining so much?
 South Florida was drenched Monday as rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms swept across the region, producing impressive rainfall totals and widespread flooding concerns. 
 At least one school, St. Bonaventure Catholic School in Davie, closed for the day due to flooding. Public schools in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach were already closed for teacher planning days on Election Day. 
 Voting has also been affected, as some polling places have had to be changed. See if your precinct is impacted here. 
 #TrafficAlert #WestonFL
Current traffic issues due to roadway flooding: 
· Indian Trace westbound between Three Village and Bonaventure is flooded.
· Bonaventure south of Lakeview is flooded all the way down to Indian Trace
· N. Commerce Parkway and Weston Road – Lights on flash
· Eastbound lane at Glades Circle and Glades Parkway shut down
· Southbound Bonaventure from Royal Poinciana to Indian Trace closed.
Do NOT drive into flooded waters.
— City of Weston (@CityofWeston) November 3, 2026 
 How much did it rain in South Florida?
 Doppler radar estimates show some neighborhoods received more than 6 inches of rain, with particularly heavy amounts across Broward County. Rainfall reports included more than 7 inches in Sunrise, around 6 inches in Weston and over 5 inches in Davie. 
 Video taken on Monday from outside Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise shows some fans who were there for the Panthers game walking out of the rink into knee-high water. In that area, estimates can go even higher, up to 9 inches. 
 Some of the heaviest downpours produced rainfall rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour, overwhelming drainage systems and leaving standing water on streets and in low-lying neighborhoods.
 Rainfall from the past 24 hours. This image is from the morning of Nov. 3, 2026. 
 So why is it raining so much in South Florida? 
 The main culprit was an upper-level area of low pressure spinning to the southwest of South Florida over the eastern Gulf of Mexico. 
 This system helped draw deep tropical moisture into our region while also providing the atmospheric lift needed to generate widespread showers and thunderstorms. Think of it as a combination of an atmosphere loaded with moisture and a weather system helping squeeze that moisture out in the form of heavy rain. 
 Persistent onshore winds supplied additional Atlantic moisture, creating an ideal environment for highly efficient, tropical-style downpours.
 Making matters worse was the slow movement of many of these storms. Instead of quickly passing through, some thunderstorms repeatedly developed over the same neighborhoods, a process called  "training." That allowed rainfall totals to climb rapidly, even while nearby communities experienced considerably less rain. The saturated ground from previous downpours only added to the flooding concerns.
 Sunrise, FL: Monday night's rain (generalized 7-9") puts it in the 1-in-50-year reoccurrence range, leaning 1-in-75-year.
While up in the Palm Bay area, it's more like 1-in-1000-year range.
As always, Florida loves to over-perform. 🌧🌧️
***h/t @NStewWX for his bag of tricks. https://t.co/i1XLOKtAS5
— Ryan Phillips - NBC6 (@RyanNBC6) November 3, 2026 
 How long will it rain in South Florida?
 The good news is that a significant change in our weather pattern is on the way! Additional showers and thunderstorms remain possible Today and Wednesday as the upper-level disturbance gradually weakens and moves away. 
 However, drier air is expected to filter into South Florida during the second half of the week. That sets the stage for a much more enjoyable weekend, with a better mix of sunshine, warm temperatures and periods of lower humidity.
 After days of soaking rain, South Florida is finally looking forward to some amazing November weather!
 U.S. Rep. Carlos Giménez to vote in person in Miami
 U.S. Rep. Carlos Giménez, who is running to keep his seat representing Florida House District 28, will vote in person at Plymouth Congregational Church, according to a news release. 
 Giménez said he would talk to the media afterward. He is running for re-election against Democrat Phil Ehr and Independent Eddie Rojas.
